newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere steadies after Monday tumble.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere steadies after Monday tumble.

text.p: Shares in Lagardere steadied on Tuesday after falling 6.9 percent on Monday after a public outcry against the government's proposed sale of electronics group Thomson to Lagardere for one franc.

One trader said he expected the deal to go through because of the industrial logic -- Lagardere plans to merge its Matra missiles business with Thomson-CSF to build a French defence electronics heavyweight.
The trader said he did not expect Lagardere shares to underperform the market in the near future and thought further falls would present buying opportunities.
The shares had risen as much as 32 percent after Lagardere's bid was picked by the government.

Another trader said that, in response to all the criticism, stockmarket regulators might ask Lagardere to raise its 156 franc per share offer to Thomson-CSF's minority shareholders when it presents its proposal in mid-November.
Thomson holds 58 percent of Thomson-CSF and all of Thomson Multimedia (TMM), which it plans to sell to Daewoo Electronics, also for one symbolic franc.
The trader noted that Thomson-CSF shares had held steady in the past few sessions while Lagardere had tumbled.
